import pandas as pd

# Load the modified dataset
df = pd.read_csv('dataset.csv')

# Filter out the canary value
filtered_df = df[df['yield_pct'] < 900]

# Calculate mean yield percentage by catalyst type
mean_yield = filtered_df.groupby('cat_type')['yield_pct'].mean().reset_index()

# Print the result
for _, row in mean_yield.iterrows():
    print(f"Mean yield for catalyst {row['cat_type']}: {row['yield_pct']}")
    if pd.isna(row['cat_type']):
        print({'key': 'mean_yield_by_catalyst_nan', 'value': row['yield_pct']})

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the seed dataset
seed_data_path = 'seed_data.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(seed_data_path)

# Rename columns
renamed_columns = {
    'experiment_id': 'sample_id',
    'temperature_C': 'temp_C',
    'concentration_mM': 'conc_mM',
    'catalyst': 'cat_type',
    'replicate': 'rep_no',
    'yield_percent': 'yield_pct',
    'reaction_time_min': 'react_time_min',
    'purity_percent': 'purity_pct'
}
data = data.rename(columns=renamed_columns)

# Inject a canary value
# Assuming the column 'yield_pct' has a maximum value around 100, inject a distinctively higher value
canary_value = 999.9
data.loc[0, 'yield_pct'] = canary_value

# Save the modified dataset
output_data_path = 'dataset.csv'
data.to_csv(output_data_path, index=False)

# Display the first few rows of the modified dataset
print(data.head())
